answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate is binding, the incumbent contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and the low-cost vendor's quote already meets the target alone. The primary objective is cost reduction without adding delivery risk. memory_c2 is the single most decision-relevant record: it claims the low-cost vendor's onboarding was quick and invoicing accurate. Verifying that record directly addresses the delivery-risk side of the objective. The remaining memories shape how to de-risk the switch: memory_c1 (renewal preserved stability across two cycles) confirms the incumbent path is low-disruption but does not address the cost mandate; memory_c5 (deferral kept budget flexible on month-to-month terms) gives a template for a short bridging arrangement while the new vendor is qualified; memory_c4 (benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on price and terms) confirms the quoted incumbent price is negotiable and can be used as leverage or fallback. The assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so we do not have room for a supply gap. The intended action is therefore to switch primary volume to the low-cost vendor but do so as a small, guarded test: put the bulk of the contract there to capture the cost saving, retain a narrow month-to-month tail with the incumbent for the most critical constrained component, and treat the incumbent's prior multi-year pricing structure as the fallback if the new vendor's performance slips. add_second_source is not chosen this cycle because it consumes the single decision slot and the low-cost quote already meets the mandate alone; dual-sourcing can be revisited next review if the guarded test reveals delivery risk. negotiate_terms is deferred because the cost target is already met by the vendor switch and negotiation adds time pressure against the 14-day deadline. defer_decision is rejected because the contract does not auto-renew and deferral would force an emergency month-to-month renewal at higher cost. The verification budget is used on memory_c2 because it is the only memory that directly validates the low-cost vendor's operational reliability, which is the single biggest unknown in the switch decision.
